title: Incompressible Box Transport and Finite Computation
main_claim: Theorem (Balanced three-stack realization): for every Turing machine and finite input there is an effective smooth force f=f0+nu f1 on R^3, with compact spatial support and one-periodic after t=1, whose zero-data Navier-Stokes solution is (U,0). The particle starting at x*=(4,0,0) enters (-1,2)^3 if and only if the machine halts. Uniqueness holds in the class CH^2 ∩ C^1L^2 with bounded u and grad u and CH^1 pressure. The geometric engine is Theorem 3.4: a box routing in which finite determinant-one positive-diagonal maps between separately disjoint rational solid boxes are realized as the time-one map of an effective compactly supported solenoidal field.
coverage:
Read introduction, analysis (comparison lemma and torus projection), geometry (curl lemma, lift/parking schedules, routing theorem) and balanced (main theorem) in full. Checks made:
- Curl identity: curl(G×y)=2G−y div G+(y·∇)G. The potential gives exactly ċ+L(x−c), using tr L=0.
- Rule table: the machine is deterministic and covers every reachable configuration (checkpoint invariant R=a1..am⋆b^∞, m≥1). Each rule preserves total prefix length (1,1,2,1,1; 2,3,3,4), so the determinant is 1.
- Source and target separation holds per control, including the distinct-κ records for A-targets and the ⋆ versus letter tops. Gapped odd-digit intervals are disjoint for incompatible prefixes, and the affine prefix map sends I(α) onto I(α').
- Routing margins: Λ-scaled separation >20R; parking offsets ≥30R; obstacle-cube detours at max-norm radius 4R leave a gap ≥2R; the expansion and contraction gaps g_a, g_b are monotone.
- No-premature-event bound x1>2: halt target cubes lie at ≤Λ+4<4Λ, and every other obstacle and endpoint is at ≥4Λ.
- Loading path, and the case where the input is already halted.
- Energy-comparison cases (i)-(v): the cutoff errors, and the gradient-pairing lemma via Fourier.
- Projection constants: the shell count 24n^2+2, S_L=(1+52(L/2π)^4)^{1/2}, d_L, the tail bound, the multinomial H^n bound and the quadrature Lipschitz constant.
Only skimmed: the later variant sections (initialization, persistent and guarded history, observer/solid/torus routing, clocks, and the imported input-offset processor).
